evidence.source: 《漢語多功能字庫》, character entry 識
evidence.field: formation; Shuowen; dated usage and semantic senses
evidence.text: The entry reports 識 as 从言、戠聲 and reproduces the 《說文》 gloss 常也、一曰知也. It identifies an early sense as “remember/retain,” citing 《周易·大畜》 君子以多識前言往行 and 《論語·述而》 默而識之. It separately gives “know/recognize,” with 《詩·大雅·皇矣》 不識不知 and 《史記·刺客列傳》 妻不識也; further senses include knowledge, consciousness/perception, flags or markers, and an acquaintance. The source’s ordering is an editorial semantic analysis; it is not a chronology established solely by its gloss list.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「識」

evidence.source: 《漢語多功能字庫》, character entry 識
evidence.text: The page displays one small-seal form and nine selected bamboo-and-silk forms, but no oracle-bone or bronze forms under 識. This entry therefore does not establish a dated early graphic form of the compound 識. Its linked 戠 analysis separately reports oracle-bone and bronze forms for 戠; those are evidence about the phonetic graph, not direct images or attestations of the compound 識.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「識」

evidence.source: 《漢語多功能字庫》, character entry 戠
evidence.text: The entry says 戠 has oracle-bone forms and proposes a graph composed of 戈 and an inverted triangular shape, interpreted as an early pictograph of 樴/杙, a pointed wooden stake; it says that shape functions as a phonetic in 戠. It reports bronze inscriptions using 戠 for 識 (“knowledge”) and also for 織. The entry reproduces 《說文》 戠，闕。从戈从音, which differs from its own proposed early graphic analysis. These are source assertions about 戠, not proof that 識 depicts a stake or that the early name of the object is independently recoverable.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「戠」

evidence.source: 《漢語多功能字庫》, character entry 識
evidence.text: The page records two 《廣韻》 fanqie spellings for 識: 職吏 and 賞職, assigning them to different Middle Chinese categories (departing-tone 章 and entering-tone 書, respectively). The distinction supports multiple historical readings; it should not be collapsed into one reading or treated as a dated semantic sequence.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「識」

evidence.source: 《漢語多功能字庫》, character entry 戠
evidence.text: 戠 is listed with a 《廣韻》 fanqie 之翼 and a Middle Chinese entering-tone, third-division reading. The same entry proposes a wooden-stake origin for the graph, reports contested interpretations of some oracle-bone uses, and says bronze 戠 can write 識 and 織. This supports reporting a historical phonetic relationship at the level of source analysis, while leaving the original stake-name pronunciation and any direct sound derivation unestablished here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「戠」

evidence.source: 《漢語多功能字庫》, character entry 只
evidence.field: modern and historical reading; graph history
evidence.text: The entry gives modern Mandarin readings through displayed pronunciation graphics and reproduces 《說文》 只 as a sentence particle, explaining its graph through 口 and a shape said to depict breath descending. Its listed 《廣韻》 fanqie readings are 章移 and 諸氏. This character has its own history and meanings; evidence here does not make 只 the historical phonetic of traditional 識.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「只」

evidence.source: 《簡化字總表》, as reproduced in a secondary reference
evidence.text: The page states that 识 is among the characters derived by applying the simplified component 只（戠） and that 戠 itself is not simplified to 只. It also describes 讠 as the simplified left-side form of 言. This supports describing 识 as the standardized simplified counterpart of 識, with the visible parts arising through component simplification; it does not support treating 只 as the historical phonetic in the traditional graph 識.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.
